heard: The first pictures of the moon's far side used American spy film. In October 1959, the Soviet Union launched Luna 3 to reveal our satellite's hidden hemisphere. Because the moon is tidally locked, humanity had never seen the side facing away from Earth. The probe carried an automated darkroom to develop, fix, and dry photographs mid-flight. On October 7, 1959, the spacecraft took 29 photographs over roughly 40 minutes. According to historical accounts, the radiation-resistant film inside the camera came from downed U.S. spy balloons. 17 frames survived transmission back to Earth, permanently altering our map of the Moon. That is how American spy film captured the first pictures of the Moon's far side.
